newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans post double-digit gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans post double-digit gains.

text.p: CBOT July soybean futures posted double-digit gains in fast trading on ideas prices needed to rise to ensure tight U.S. soybean supplies will last through the summer, traders said.

Thursday's National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure supported ideas demand was running too fast for existing supplies. NOPA put the crush at roughly 25 million bushels, above trade expectations.
Domestic demand for soy products and continued strong exports further fueled supply concerns.

Cash soymeal basis levels continued to rise on Friday despite the crush level, cash sources said. Merchants said end-users were covering June and July positions and processors were having trouble sourcing soybeans.
At 1040 CDT, soybeans were up 11 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel with July up 11 at $8.88 a bushel. Soymeal was up $3.50 to $1.00 per ton with July up $3.50 at $287.40 a ton.
